chunks: He said: Abu Ubaidullah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me, saying: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hakimi reported to us, saying: Ismail ibn Ishaq al-Qadhi reported to us, saying: Saeed ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Saeed, saying: Abdul Malik ibn Umair al-Lakhmi narrated to us, saying:

Once Jariya ibn Qudamah al-Sa'di called upon Mu'awiyah; and upon the throne, there were al-Ahnaf ibn Qais and al-Habbab al-Majashee sitting next to him. Mu'awiyah said to him: "Who are you?" He replied: "I am Jariya ibn Qudamah." And he was among the nobles. Mu'awiyah said to him: "May be so, but are you anything but a bee?" He said: "O Mu'awiyah, do not do that! You have compared me to a bee. By Allah, it has a fierce sting and sweet honey. And by Allah, Mu'awiyah is nothing but a female dog howling at other dogs! And Umayyah is nothing but the diminutive of Amah - a slave-woman." Mu'awiyah said: "Do not do that!" He said: "You did it, so I did likewise." He said to him: "Then come closer and sit with me on the throne." He said: "I will not do that." He asked: "Why?" He replied: "Because I see that these two have displaced you from your seat, and I would not join them." Mu'awiyah said to him: "Come closer so I may confide in you." So he drew near, and he said to him: "O Jariya, I have bought from these two their faith." He said: "Then buy from me too, O Mu'awiyah." He said to him: "Do not speak loudly."

key_terms.أُمَّة: slave-woman - Jariya's wordplay showing 'Umayyah' is the diminutive of 'Amah'
key_terms.دِين: faith/religion - What Mu'awiyah confessed to purchasing from his two courtiers
key_terms.سَرِير: throne - The seat of power where Mu'awiyah sat with his courtiers
key_terms.كَلْبَة: female dog - Jariya's retort on the etymology of 'Mu'awiyah' as a howling female dog
key_terms.نَحْلَة: bee - Mu'awiyah's insult comparing Jariya to a bee, implying insignificance

ai.seo_question: What happened when Jariya ibn Qudamah al-Sa'di visited Mu'awiyah's court and was insulted?
ai.summary: Jariya ibn Qudamah al-Sa'di, a noble Arab, visited Mu'awiyah's court where al-Ahnaf ibn Qais and al-Habbab al-Majashee were seated on the throne beside him. When Mu'awiyah insulted Jariya by calling him a mere bee, Jariya retorted with devastating wordplay: a bee has a strong sting and sweet honey, while 'Mu'awiyah' literally means a female dog howling at other dogs, and 'Umayyah' is the diminutive of 'Amah' (a slave-woman). After the exchange, Mu'awiyah privately confessed to Jariya that he had bought the faith of his two courtiers, revealing the corruption at the heart of his political power.
